summary: Tested Merch Drop + Stripe checkout end-to-end. Backend: 8/8 pytest passed (public /api/merch shows seeded 'Good Mood Tee — Vol.1' at 3500 EUR cents with populated stripe_product_id/stripe_price_id/lookup_key 'gm_*'; POST /api/payments/checkout returns valid https://checkout.stripe.com/ URL + cs_ session id; invalid lookup_key -> 404; /api/payments/status/{sid} returns pending payment_status with correct amount_cents=price*qty and currency=eur; /api/admin/merch requires Bearer (401 without); /api/admin/orders includes the created session; full CRUD cycle: create -> appears in public list -> update price triggers new stripe_price_id (old deactivated) -> delete removes from public list). Frontend: nav-merch link scrolls to #merch, merch-section visible, size buttons S/M/L/XL, qty +/- steppers, total updates in € (35€ -> 70€), BUY NOW POSTs and redirects to checkout.stripe.com/... /payment/cancel -> cancel-back-merch returns to /#merch. /payment/success shows 'CONFIRMING PAYMENT' loader then 'STILL PROCESSING' when session unknown. Admin login works; all 5 tabs (Catalogue, Tour, Store, Orders, Newsletter) present; Orders tab renders 3 pending transactions with product lookup_key, size/qty, EUR amounts, pending status. No real Stripe payment completed.

issues: Product column displays raw lookup_key (e.g. 'gm_6cd0e42f') instead of product name — cosmetic; consider joining with products collection for readability

critical_code_review_comments: server.py now ~600 lines — approaching the 700-line split threshold; consider modularizing (routers/merch.py, routers/payments.py) before further growth.

_sync_product_to_stripe is a sync function called from async endpoints — blocking the event loop on every Stripe API round-trip. Acceptable for admin CRUD but should ideally use stripe async client or asyncio.to_thread.
Merch seed on startup wraps Stripe sync in bare except Exception — if Stripe is temporarily down at boot the product is silently skipped. Consider retry or explicit log level ERROR.
AdminDashboard.jsx (~511 lines) and product/volume/tour form components all in one file — split into per-tab modules for maintainability.
Orders table shows lookup_key instead of product name — join or embed product snapshot in payment_transactions for better UX and historical accuracy.
seed_data_creation: Backend startup seeds 1 product 'Good Mood Tee — Vol.1' (35€) with Stripe sync; 3 test checkout sessions were created during backend tests and are visible in Admin Orders.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Stripe test keys live in /app/backend/.env. Do NOT complete real payments. Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/test_merch_payments.py covers full CRUD + payments status. Multiple pending test sessions persist in db.payment_transactions from prior runs (unique index on session_id keeps them de-duped).
